sources.title: Giant Ground Sloths: Shasta Ground Sloth
sources.author: National Park Service
sources.evidence: Approximate9ft length, long slender skull/narrow mouth, large foreclaws; species-level size not particular fossil measurement.

sources.title: The Human Footprint: Giant Ground Sloth
sources.author: Yale Peabody Museum, photograph Andy Melien
sources.evidence: Current YPM VP013198 exhibit photo inspected; preserved skin/fur/ligaments stated. Collection detail link returned403, not used.
sources.rights: Yale/Andy Melien copyright, private reference only.

sources.title: Nothrotheriops skeleton
sources.author: Jesse Earl Hyde Collection, CWRU, historical photo
sources.evidence: Actual partially mummified Yale specimen viewed, supports small long skull, differentiated limbs, tail and preserved claws. Historical restoration limitations apply.
sources.rights: Public domain in US per source; private unmodified reference, no scan mesh reused.

sources.title: Designing scientifically-grounded paleoart for augmented reality at La Brea Tar Pits
sources.author: Davis and colleagues (2022)
sources.evidence: YPM13198 and Lull posture reference; five skin patches, one with45mm pale-yellowhair. External digit proportions uncertain; their face pattern is artistic, not evidence. No published lowpoly geometry or artwork copied.

sources.title: A new genus and species of nothrotheriid sloth from Peru
sources.author: De Iuliis, Gaudin and Vicars (2011)
sources.evidence: Comparative Nothrotheriops manual anatomy: digitV reduced/no claw; Lull fifth-finger restoration likely misplaced digitI. II ungual longer thanIII; III/IV near equal. Do not substitute Mionothropus wholebody.

sources.title: Large Mammalian Clawed Herbivores: A Comparative Study
sources.author: Margery Coombs (1983)
sources.evidence: Author-posted text describes Nothrotheriops long slender forelimbs relative to hindlimbs and pedolateral hindfoot support.
sources.rights: American Philosophical Society; private research only

sources.title: A remarkable ground sloth
sources.author: Richard Swann Lull (1929), Yale University Press
sources.evidence: Original p9 table viewed: YPM13198 maxilla-occipital287+mm,muzzle59.5mm. pp15-16 and PlateVI true preserved pes: III largest claw,II intermediate,IV smaller; vestigialV no claw and hallux lost. PlateV rightmanus inspected. Later2011 correction supersedes old leftmanualV interpretation.
sources.rights: 1929 published historical work, public domain US; private reference pages.
